## Short answer

The premise is half right: Sanic *does* use the standard mechanisms — PEP 508 environment markers for the platform/interpreter condition, and `extras_require` for genuinely optional add-ons. The `SANIC_NO_UJSON` / `SANIC_NO_UVLOOP` environment variables are not a substitute for those; they are a **subtractive, build-time opt-out**, which neither extras nor markers can express: extras are additive-only, and Sanic's design contract is that the accelerators are installed by default (its own description is "Build fast. Run fast.", `setup.py:76–79`).

---

## What the code actually does

`setup.py` @ `57d44f2`:

```python
env_dependency = '; sys_platform != "win32" ' 'and implementation_name == "cpython"'
ujson = "ujson>=1.35" + env_dependency
uvloop = "uvloop>=0.15.0" + env_dependency
types_ujson = "types-ujson" + env_dependency
requirements = ["sanic-routing>=23.12.0", "httptools>=0.0.10", uvloop, ujson, ...]
```
— [`setup.py:97–112`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/setup.py#L97-L112)

```python
if str_to_bool(os.environ.get("SANIC_NO_UJSON", "no")):
    print("Installing without uJSON")
    requirements.remove(ujson)
    tests_require.remove(types_ujson)

# 'nt' means windows OS
if str_to_bool(os.environ.get("SANIC_NO_UVLOOP", "no")):
    print("Installing without uvLoop")
    requirements.remove(uvloop)
```
— [`setup.py:151–159`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/setup.py#L151-L159)

So three distinct mechanisms are in play, each doing a different job:

| Mechanism | Where | Job |
|---|---|---|
| PEP 508 markers (`; sys_platform != "win32" and implementation_name == "cpython"`) | `setup.py:97` | *Declarative* conditionality: never install these on Windows (uvloop has no Windows support) or on PyPy |
| `extras_require` | `setup.py:161–168` | Additive features: `test`, `dev`, `docs`, `all`, `ext` (`sanic-ext`), `http3` (`aioquic`) |
| `SANIC_NO_*` env vars | `setup.py:151–159` | Subtractive opt-out from a dependency that is otherwise unconditional |

`str_to_bool()` ([`setup.py:39–57`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/setup.py#L39-L57)) accepts `y/yes/true/on/1/…`, i.e. it is deliberately a friendly boolean switch rather than an exact-match check.

---

## Why not just put them in an extra?

1. **Extras cannot subtract.** `pip install sanic[test]` only *adds* distributions to `install_requires`; PEP 508 has no "minus" operator and pip has no "without" flag. Making `uvloop`/`ujson` skippable therefore requires mutating `install_requires` at metadata-generation time — the only input available there is the build environment.
2. **Default-on is a product decision, not an oversight.** If they lived in `sanic[perf]`, the plain `pip install sanic` of every user (and of every transitive dependent, whose `install_requires` rarely bothers with extras) would silently lose uvloop and ujson — the exact reason people pick Sanic. Opt-*out* keeps the fast path as the default while still allowing an escape hatch.
3. **The runtime is already tolerant of their absence**, which is what makes an install-time opt-out safe: `try_use_uvloop()` catches `ImportError` and continues on the default asyncio loop ([`sanic/server/loop.py:23–34`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/sanic/server/loop.py#L23-L34)), and it no-ops with a warning on Windows (`loop.py:13–21`). ujson is likewise an accelerator over the stdlib JSON path — an implementation detail of the release, not a public API promise, so it must not be allowed to break installation on a platform where a wheel is missing.
4. **Environment markers can't express "this environment can't/shouldn't build it."** Markers key on static facts (OS, Python version, implementation). They cannot express "no musllinux/ARM wheel exists yet for this new CPython", "this index is air-gapped and mirrors only vetted packages", or "we are a distro/conda packager who builds uvloop ourselves". A build-time env var is the standard channel for exactly that kind of local intent.

---

## The runtime half of the story

The same variable name is consulted again at runtime, but only informationally:

```python
uvloop_install_removed = str_to_bool(getenv("SANIC_NO_UVLOOP", "no"))
if uvloop_install_removed:
    error_logger.info(
        "You are requesting to run Sanic using uvloop, but the install-time "
        "'SANIC_NO_UVLOOP' environment variable (used to opt-out of installing "
        "uvloop with Sanic) is set to true. If you want to prevent Sanic from "
        "overriding the event loop policy during runtime, set the 'USE_UVLOOP' "
        "configuration value to false."
    )
if not isinstance(asyncio.get_event_loop_policy(), uvloop.EventLoopPolicy):
    asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(uvloop.EventLoopPolicy())
```
— [`sanic/server/loop.py:36–46`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/sanic/server/loop.py#L36-L46)

Note the semantics precisely: there is no `return` in that `if` block. If uvloop happens to be installed anyway (pulled in by another dependency), `SANIC_NO_UVLOOP=1` only logs — the policy is still installed. The variable's real effect is on the *metadata*; the runtime switch for loop selection is the `USE_UVLOOP` config value, which the message above (and the Windows warning) point users at.

## Practical consequences

- **Set it at build time, from an sdist.** `SANIC_NO_UVLOOP=1 SANIC_NO_UJSON=1 pip install --no-binary sanic sanic`. A PyPI wheel already has its `METADATA` baked, so the variable is a no-op there; conversely pip's wheel cache can reuse a previously built wheel that ignored a different setting, so use `--no-cache-dir` when the flag matters.
- **Both flags are exercised in CI**, which is the clearest statement of intent: `tox.ini` declares `{py38,…,pyNightly,pypp310}-no-ext` environments and sets `SANIC_NO_UJSON=1` / `SANIC_NO_UVLOOP=1` for them ([`tox.ini:2`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/tox.ini#L2), [`tox.ini:7–8`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/tox.ini#L7-L8)) so the pure-Python fallback is continuously tested. "Install with a flag" is a per-build configuration — exactly what extras can't do.
- **Cost of the approach:** the dependency set becomes a function of the build environment, so a wheel is no longer a self-contained description of what will be installed; and the opt-out is invisible to a user who installs from a wheel.
- **Minor asymmetry worth knowing:** `types_ujson` is removed only from the `test` extra. `dev_require` and `all_require` are built as *copies* before the mutation ([`setup.py:143`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/setup.py#L143), [`setup.py:149`](https://github.com/sanic-org/sanic/blob/57d44f263fa84bd5cd6f77b5565825640d85b1e2/setup.py#L149)), so `pip install sanic[dev]`/`[all]` with `SANIC_NO_UJSON=1` still pulls the stubs (harmless, since they carry the same non-Windows/CPython marker).
- **Performance, not correctness, is what you give up:** without uvloop Sanic runs on the stock asyncio loop; without ujson it uses the stdlib JSON encoder/decoder. Neither is a supported-API change, which is why a build-time escape hatch is an acceptable design.
